The Blueprint for a Real Party
The primary task of the 1903 Congress was not just to agree on a program, but to forge an
actual party. Lenin and the Iskra editorial board arrived with a clear mandate: eradicate
circle politics and implement strict organizational centralism to survive a state of siege.

After: Strict Centralism

When the Congress rejected the Bund's demand for autonomy, 7 anti-Iskra-ist delegates
walked out. In an instant, the heavy weight of the opportunist alliance vanished. Lenin's
faction became the Bolsheviki (Majority), and Martov's the Mensheviki (Minority).

The Double Knot
Ideological
Unity
Structural
Enforcement
Paragraph 1 was a crack in the pot of the Party. Lenin realized that programmatic
agreement means nothing without the organizational machinery to enforce it. The
Double Knot represents the synthesis of Marxist theory with uncompromising,
centralized party architecture. Without the structure, the ideology dissolves.

One Step Forward, Two Steps Back
One Step Forward: Uniting around
a revolutionary program and
disciplined party architecture.
Two Steps Back: The minority's refusal to
accept democratic defeat, retreating into
organizational chaos and circle mentality.
TAKEAWAY: The Bolshevik-Menshevik split was not an accident of personality,
but a fundamental divide over whether a political party is a disciplined
engine for revolution, or a broad, passive reflection of societal discontent NotebookiM
